title: Learning Chemotherapy Drug Action via Universal Physics-Informed Neural Networks

content.abstract_summary: Applies Universal Physics-Informed Neural Networks (UPINNs) to learn unknown components of pharmacodynamic ODE models for chemotherapy — the gray-box identification problem in oncology PK/PD. Demonstrates on three standard chemotherapeutic drug action models (log-kill, Norton-Simon, and a third model) using synthetic data, then learns the net proliferation rate in a doxorubicin pharmacodynamics model. The UPINN framework uses the neural network as a universal approximator for unknown ODE terms while the known mechanistic structure constrains the solution space. University of Waterloo, 2025.
key_findings: UPINN successfully learns three standard chemotherapeutic drug action terms (log-kill, Norton-Simon, and a third form) from synthetic data — demonstrates that physics-informed ML can recover known ODE structure from data without a priori specification
Parameter fitting for multiple synthetic datasets simultaneously is demonstrated — multi-experiment training with shared mechanistic structure
Net proliferation rate in doxorubicin PD model successfully learned — a real pharmacological unknown that standard ODE parameterization cannot capture
The approach occupies the exact gray-box niche: known mechanistic ODE scaffold (cell kill kinetics) + neural network to learn unknown term (proliferation rate function)
Authors explicitly frame these as 'toy examples' and 'highlight the usefulness' rather than clinical validation — honest scope statement
limitations: All validation is on synthetic data — 'toy examples' by authors' own description; clinical validation is not provided
Does not address identifiability of the learned neural network term — the UPINN may fit multiple solutions equally well
No comparison against standard ODE parameter estimation (e.g., NONMEM/Monolix) on the same data — only internal UPINN performance reported

extracted_claims.text: "As the examples we study are only toy examples, we highlight the usefulness of UPINNs in learning unknown terms in pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic models."

We show that the UPINN can successfully learn the hidden terms and unknown parameters in a variety of differential equations (with differing time and variable scales) that model the effect of chemotherapeutics on cancer cells.

gaps_addressed: Fills the UPINN slot in M1.1 — a specific form of physics-informed hybrid where a neural network learns an unknown ODE term while the rest of the mechanistic structure is fixed; directly relevant to M1.4 (when do hybrids help: when a term in the ODE is unknown but the scaffold is known)

Doxorubicin application connects to M4.1 (generative AI for pharmacometrics): UPINNs can be viewed as constrained generative models for ODE terms, where the physics constraint is the known mechanistic scaffold

provenance.notes: Found via PubMed search 'physics-informed neural network drug pharmacology' (PMID 40244511). Pharmaceutical Research 2025, 42(4):593-612.
